approved_angle.title: The time between booking a venue tour and arriving deserves a plan
approved_angle.core_perspective: When a couple schedules a tour a few weeks away, there's an opportunity to help them picture their wedding before they arrive. We look at what happens during that wait, including the emails they receive and where a personal conversation would help.

strategic_purpose.why_now: Makes pre-consult nurture tangible for venue owners and shows how LeadLock and The Foolproof Follow-Up Advantage support the owner's personal sales conversations. The caption carries the Instagram offer invitation; the Reel and carousel build the case.

audience.who: Venue owners already investing in marketing who want to carry a couple's interest from discovery through to the venue tour.
audience.reason_to_care: Once a tour is scheduled, it's natural to focus on confirmation and reminders. This piece asks what else could help couples picture their wedding and become more familiar with the venue while they wait.

body.wia_perspective:
When a couple books a venue tour a few weeks away, we look at what they receive while they wait and where a personal conversation could help. There's an opportunity to show them more of the wedding they could have there, before they arrive.

We recommend giving that couple something useful to explore: wedding footage, an invitation to ask questions or an earlier phone or virtual connection with the owner. Confirmation and reminders handle the practical details. The rest of the follow-up can help the couple become more familiar with the venue and the people behind it.

That's how we approach nurture. Automated emails and texts support the owner's sales conversation and create opportunities for personal connection.

supporting_example.scene: In a conversation about venue follow-up, our team proposed taking a closer look at the language in the messages between inquiry and tour, with particular attention to making them more personal.
supporting_example.wia_move: Whitney suggested offering an earlier phone or virtual connection. Our team also proposed a supplemental email with wedding footage and an invitation to ask questions for couples with a longer wait before their visit.
supporting_example.client_contribution: The discussion brought the tour calendar into our thinking: what could a couple experience before arriving, even when the in-person visit stays on its scheduled date?

reels.script:
What does a couple get to experience between booking a tour and walking through your doors?

If their visit is a few weeks away, there's an opportunity to help them picture their wedding before they arrive.

We were talking about venue follow-up, and our team proposed looking more closely at the language in the messages between inquiry and tour. How could those messages feel more personal?

Whitney suggested offering a phone or virtual connection before the in-person visit, so the couple could get a better idea of what to expect and have a conversation with the owner.

Our team also suggested a supplemental email for couples with a longer wait. It could include footage from weddings at the venue and an invitation to ask questions.

That gives the couple something to explore beyond the appointment details. They can see the space being used for a wedding and start thinking about what their own day could look like there.

We want automated follow-up to support those personal conversations. When we look at the time before a tour, we're thinking about what would be useful to the couple and where a connection with the owner would help.

slides.job: Introduce the opportunity through the couple's experience.
slides.text:
Give couples a glimpse of their wedding before they arrive.

When a venue tour is a few weeks away, the time before it can include more than appointment details. You can give couples something to explore, a way to ask questions and an opportunity to get to know you.

slides.job: Show the WIA question behind the recommendations.
slides.text:
We look at what couples receive between inquiry and tour.

In a venue follow-up conversation, our team proposed reviewing the language in those messages and where they could feel more personal. The question was what would give the couple something useful to engage with while waiting for their visit.

slides.job: Establish the practical role of reminders and the additional opportunity.
slides.text:
Confirmation and reminders have a clear job.

They tell couples when to arrive, where to go and what to expect from the appointment. Alongside those details, there's room to help them imagine the wedding itself. Think about what they could see before they ever walk through the doors.

slides.job: Make the supplemental email recommendation specific.
slides.text:
A wedding-footage email gives them something to explore.

For couples with a longer wait, our team suggested an additional email showing weddings at the venue. Footage can help them picture how the space feels when it's being used for a celebration. Include an invitation to ask questions so there's a natural way to continue the conversation.

slides.job: Credit Whitney and explain the personal connection.
slides.text:
An earlier conversation can sit alongside the in-person tour.

Whitney suggested offering a phone or virtual connection before the visit. It's an opportunity to answer questions and give couples a closer look at what they can expect. The scheduled tour can stay on the calendar while the relationship has a chance to begin sooner.

slides.job: Keep the recommendation workable for the owner.
slides.text:
Build the plan around how your venue operates.

Consider what can be shared through email and where a personal conversation would be useful. Wedding footage gives couples something they can watch in their own time. An invitation to connect gives you another way to help them prepare for the visit, without changing the in-person tour date.

slides.job: Name the offer and preserve its broader scope.
slides.text:
This is part of the follow-up work we build.

LeadLock is the platform. The Foolproof Follow-Up Advantage is the automated email and text system we set up in it. It includes inquiry nurture, consult booking and reminders, pre-consult nurture and post-consult follow-up, supporting the conversations you have with couples along the way.

slides.job: Close on the division of work and the couple's experience.
slides.text:
You stay at the centre of the conversation.

The follow-up system sends the emails and texts. You answer the couple's questions, offer the personal connection and lead the tour. Together, those touchpoints give couples more to engage with before they arrive and give you a more thoughtful way to prepare for meeting them.

email.preview: Wedding footage and an earlier conversation can give couples something useful to engage with while they wait.
email.opening:
Hi {{contact.first_name}},

A couple has chosen a date to visit your venue. If that visit is a few weeks away, you have time to help them get a clearer picture of the wedding they could have there.
email.body:
The confirmation email handles the appointment details. Reminders help them prepare for the visit. Alongside those practical messages, there's an opportunity to show them more of the venue and invite a conversation.

This came up in a discussion about venue follow-up. Our team proposed looking more closely at the language in the messages between inquiry and tour, particularly where they could feel more personal.

Whitney suggested offering an earlier phone or virtual connection. That would give couples a chance to speak with the owner and get a better idea of what to expect before the in-person visit.

Our team also proposed an additional email for couples whose tour was further away, with wedding footage and an invitation to ask questions. Seeing a celebration at the venue gives them something concrete to explore as they think about their own wedding.

Those are useful questions to ask about the time before a tour: what could the couple see, what might they want to ask and where would a personal connection help?

That's how we think about automated nurture. We want the emails and texts to support the conversations you have with couples.

LeadLock is the platform, and The Foolproof Follow-Up Advantage is the follow-up system we build in it. We set up automated email and text workflows for inquiry nurture, consult booking and reminders, pre-consult nurture and post-consult follow-up. You continue to lead the personal conversations, answer questions and help couples decide whether your venue is the right fit.

The weeks before a tour are one part of that experience worth giving some thought.
email.ending:
If you'd like to explore LeadLock for your venue, simply reply to this email and let's talk about your business.

Daniela & Whitney

caption.hook: There's more to a tour confirmation than a date on the calendar.
caption.body:
You've invested in helping the right couples discover your venue. Once they've scheduled a visit, you have another opportunity to help them get to know it.

For a couple whose tour is a few weeks away, consider what would be useful during that time. They could watch footage of a wedding at the venue, ask a question or have a phone or virtual conversation with you before arriving.

In a venue follow-up discussion, Whitney suggested that earlier personal connection. Our team also proposed an extra email with wedding footage for couples with a longer wait. Both ideas give the couple a way to engage beyond the appointment logistics.

That's the thinking behind the nurture we build. LeadLock is the platform, and The Foolproof Follow-Up Advantage is the automated email and text system we set up in it, from inquiry nurture and consult reminders to follow-up after the conversation.

The system supports your personal contact with couples. You still answer their questions, lead the tour and help them decide whether they can picture their wedding there.
caption.ending: DM us "ADS" to inquire about LeadLock for your venue.

Keeping the Instagram offer invitation in the caption gives the Reel and carousel room to establish the value without repeating the ask.
